title: Session-aware microbatch planner with eviction-tagged KV slots
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design and implement a microbatch planner that forms streaming chat batches with session-awareness, and annotates KV cache slots with eviction tags to guide slab-aware eviction and prefetching. Goal: maintain sub-120ms tail latency for streaming first-byte while increasing throughput by 12-20% and reducing peak GPU memory pressure under mixed-length chat workloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Planner forms microbatches respecting per-session latency SLOs and token-priority weights; 2) KV slots are tagged with (session-age, reuse-prob, hotness-score) and used by eviction daemon to produce <10% extra eviction churn; 3) End-to-end e2e perf: median latency unchanged, 95th percentile latency for streaming first-byte <= 120ms at 80% utilization; 4) Integration tests for streaming flush, prefetch correctness, and fallback to non-tagged eviction.
implementation_notes: Planner uses a prioritized token budget per microbatch: latency-sensitive sessions get token-weight boost to reduce queuing; throughput sessions are accumulated up to slab thresholds.

KV slot tags stored in lightweight sidecar metadata (non-blocking update path) to avoid write amplification during decode. Tags: session_age_bucket, reuse_prob (LRU-smoothed), token_density_estimate, last_access_seq.
Eviction daemon uses a two-pass slab-aware algorithm: first score slots by (tag-weighted hotness) then pick contiguous slab segments to minimize fragmented GPU memory churn.
Prefetch heuristic: when forming microbatch, planner predicts KV footprint of top-K sessions and schedules DMA-prefetch for slabs with >threshold reuse_prob.
Streaming flush policy: emit partial tokens when earliest-request latency nears SLO; allow microbatch to complete remaining tokens in background but keep KV pinned until completion or explicit evict.
Fallback: if prefetch misses or memory shortfall occurs, fall back to conservative LRU eviction with immediate slab compaction and mark session as "requeue_low_priority" for routing.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — simulated microbatch planner prototype implemented in Rust harness. Verified token-weight logic reduces queuing for pinned sessions in synthetic workload.
2026-03-05: Early benchmarks show 15% throughput gain but 8% increased eviction churn when using naive per-slot tagging. Identified fragmentation as root cause.
2026-03-07: Decided on slab-aware two-pass eviction to trade contiguous frees for slightly higher compute overhead (measured compute <1% of total runtime).
2026-03-09: Diego pushed PR #1289 with initial planner + tag propagation; CI flaky on streaming tests — investigating race in sidecar metadata updates.

2026-03-11: Resolved race by switching sidecar updates to atomic compare-and-swap and introducing per-session sequence stamps. Re-ran benchmarks: eviction churn down to 6%, 95p latency at 118ms under 80% util.
2026-03-12: Code review comments from PM + SRE: add canary rollouts, expose tagging tuning knobs in console, and add integration test for on-prem private deployments with limited GPU memory.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Patel): Ensure knobs are surfaced in Console Optimize tab; prefer conservative defaults for enterprise customers with stricter SLOs.
Design (Lina Park): Suggest enriching tag with 'pinned_until' to prevent premature eviction during streaming flush windows.
SRE (Omar Chen): Add observability: 'eviction_reasons', 'slab_fragmentation', and 'prefetch_hit_rate' metrics; require alerts for sustained prefetch_miss_rate>10%.
Security (Nina Rao): Verify sidecar metadata doesn't leak PII — tags must use hashed session IDs and no raw prompt snippets.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tagging metadata updates could create contention on hot sessions -> Mitigation: use lock-free per-session ring buffer for updates and batch sidecar writes.
Risk: Prefetching increases PCIe traffic and could saturate interconnect -> Mitigation: limit concurrent prefetch DMA to a tunable window and measure pcie_utilization in e2e tests.
Risk: Slab compaction is compute-heavy -> Mitigation: schedule compaction during low-utilization windows and limit compaction band per-minute.
qa_plan: Unit tests for tag numeric stability and atomic updates.
Integration tests: streaming chat e2e with simulated prefetch miss, verify flush semantics and final completion correctness.
Perf regression suite comparing baseline batching to session-aware planner across 10 workload mixes.
Chaos test: kill eviction daemon mid-compaction to ensure benign recovery and no GPU memory leaks.
deployment_plan: Canary rollout to dedicated cluster 'dedicated-us-west-1-canary' with 2-hour ramp and continuous SLO monitoring.
Expose tuning knobs in Redwood Console: 'session_weight', 'prefetch_concurrency', 'slab_compaction_rate'.
If 95p latency > 130ms or slab_fragmentation alert triggers, automatically rollback to baseline batcher and alert on-call.

Follow-up tickets expected: tuning UI for Optimize, on-prem packaging validation, and research on RL-based eviction scoring.
